newsitem.title: ITALY: Analysts positive on Magneti Marelli.
newsitem.headline: Analysts positive on Magneti Marelli.

text.p: Analysts said they were positive about prospects for Italian automotive components group Magneti Marelli after the Fiat unit gave upbeat forecasts.

At a meeting with analysts on Tuesday night, Magneti said it expected turnover of around 8.0 trillion lire, against 5.806 trillion in 1996, and return on sales of above five percent, versus 2.7 percent, in the years 1999/2000.
The group also aimed to bring return on investment to around the average levels of its competitors, at 19-20 percent compared to the current 11 percent.
Magneti also told analysts it aimed to boost its European market share and to emerging markets. It noted sales to German firms rose 60 percent in 1996 to 6-7 percent of turnover.
It also aimed for a drastic reduction in fixed and structural costs.

Magneti posted 1996 consolidated net profit of 58 billion lire against 54 billion on sales up 4.6 percent on 1995. First quarter 1997 group sales rose 6.1 percent to 1.62 trillion lire with pre-tax profit of nine billion lire.

"The targets are very ambitious. I prefer to remain cautious about 1997 given strong competitor pressure," said Monica Bosio, analyst at Eptasim brokers. "Nevertheless, we reckon the aggressiveness shown by the company can underpin share prices in the short term. We advise a Hold and some trading purchases."

"From a stock market point of view Magneti Marelli is cheaper than Fiat so we advise switching," said Gianluca Pediconi of Milla Sim. "The price/earnings ratio is in line with competitors and if we compare price to cash flow the multiples become some of the most interesting in Italy and Europe.
"We therefore confirm an Accumulate," he said.
At 1102 GMT, Magneti stock was up 4.47 percent at 2,615 lire in active trade while Fiat shares were up 1.49 percent at 5,590 lire on a firmer Milan stock market.
